primitives.name: Temporal train/validation/test split as anti-leakage invariant
primitives.verbatim_quote: The data was divided using a temporal split to prevent data leakage and to simulate real-world forecasting: Training (70%): Earliest seasons used for model learning; Validation (15%): Middle period used for hyperparameter tuning; Test (15%): Most recent season(s) used for final, unbiased evaluation; and Stratification: Ensured the distribution of wins, draws, and losses remained consistent across all three sets.
primitives.assumptions: As printed (PDF p.4, journal p.247): matches are chronologically ordered; earliest seasons train, middle period tunes, most recent seasons test; stratification keeps win/draw/loss proportions consistent across the three sets, which implicitly assumes class-proportion stationarity across seasons. No formula is printed for the split itself.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Temporal ordering alone does not prevent leakage if rolling features are computed across the split boundary or if post-match columns (e.g., full-time goals) enter the feature matrix. Stratifying a temporal split forces class balance across non-overlapping eras and breaks under regime change (transfers, coaching changes, rule changes) — the paper itself flags league volatility on PDF p.2. The 70/15/15 proportions are asserted, not justified against season boundaries.
timescales: tau_2 = rolling feature window (3-10 matches, weeks)
tau_3 = season (~9 months, 38 matchdays per club)
split boundary = season-scale cut between train/validation/test

layer2.mapping: The temporal split is the same invariant as GSE held-out discipline: no fit is scored on its own training rows. In the 22-player football dynamical system, the outcome transition kernel P(outcome | state) may only be evaluated on states whose timestamp is strictly later than every row used to fit it. The split binds to the information-boundary constraint on the state estimator, not to any particular classifier.
layer2.telemetry: Match-date timestamps and feature-computation timestamps per row; an availability audit proving every feature value was observable strictly before kickoff of the predicted match; per-season class proportions to test the stratification stationarity assumption.

primitives.name: Multi-scale rolling form features plus days-since-last-match fatigue proxy
primitives.verbatim_quote: To calculate rolling averages, performance indicators such as goals, shots, and possession were calculated over the last 3, 5, and 10 matches. Strength Metrics rating of dynamic skill levels, such as attack/defence ratios, and head-to-head historical statistics, were considered.
primitives.assumptions: As printed (PDF p.4, journal p.247): rolling averages over the last 3, 5, and 10 matches for goals, shots, possession; attack/defence ratios and head-to-head statistics as strength metrics; contextual factors include home-ground advantage and 'days since last match' to capture fatigue. Implicit assumptions: recent matches are informative about a latent team-strength state (weak stationarity within a 3-10 match window); days since last match is a sufficient scalar proxy for recovery; home advantage is stable. No formula is printed for the rolling kernel.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Short windows (3) are high-variance; long windows (10) go stale after transfers, injuries, or coaching changes — the paper's own stated failure mode of static models (PDF p.2). Days-since-last-match ignores travel distance, circadian disruption, and within-match physical load, so it cannot distinguish a rested squad from a rested-but-bruised one. Possession is style-dependent, not strength-dependent: a low-block team can be strong while averaging low possession.
timescales: tau_1 = single match (~5400 s of play)
tau_2 = rolling windows of 3, 5, 10 matches (~1-8 weeks)

layer2.mapping: The 3/5/10-match rolling averages are a multi-scale low-pass observation kernel on the latent team-strength state of the 22-player system: each window length is a bias-variance setting on the same hidden state. Days-since-last-match binds to a recovery/fatigue state variable that gates the transition kernel (a fatigued squad's effective strength is discounted before outcome probabilities are computed). In GSE's Coach-Mind sim the identical structure appears as rolling opponent-tendency priors plus a fatigue gate on play-call EV.
layer2.telemetry: Per-match event streams (goals, shots, possession) to fit window weights; minutes played, GPS high-speed running distance, and travel logs to calibrate the days-since-match proxy against actual physical load; head-to-head records are sparse and need shrinkage toward the league prior.

primitives.name: Random Forest bagging variance reduction with probabilistic three-way output
primitives.verbatim_quote: Random Forest, a bagging method that aggregates predictions from multiple independent decision trees to reduce variance and improve generalisation.
primitives.assumptions: As printed (PDF p.4, journal p.247): bagging aggregates multiple independent decision trees to reduce variance; models were 'configured to output probabilities for each outcome (Home Win, Draw, Away Win) rather than simple labels'; XGBoost uses built-in regularisation and early stopping on validation performance. Implicit: trees are approximately independent (diversity from feature randomness), and vote fractions are treated as outcome probabilities. The paper cites Breiman (2001), Random forests, Machine Learning 45(1):5-32, as the algorithmic lineage (reference 4, PDF p.9).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Random Forest vote fractions are not calibrated posterior probabilities; the paper reports no calibration curve, Brier score, or reliability diagram, so the probability outputs cannot be trusted for decision weighting without a calibration layer. When one feature dominates (e.g., a leaked full-time column), trees become correlated and the independence assumption behind variance reduction fails. The draw class is the structurally hard class in three-way football prediction and is where ensemble overconfidence concentrates.

layer2.mapping: The probability simplex over {Home Win, Draw, Away Win} is isomorphic to GSE's LINE-FREE outcome distribution: a full distribution over result states, never a single pick and never an odds-derived input. Bagging's variance reduction maps to averaging independent Coach-Mind simulation draws: ensemble spread shrinks as independent scenario count grows, and correlated scenarios (shared tendency priors) break the same independence assumption.
layer2.telemetry: Reliability diagrams and Brier score on the temporal test season; per-class confusion counts (especially draw recall); ensemble spread across trees as an uncertainty proxy; calibration must be re-verified after every retrain.

primitives.name: Printed evaluation metric suite: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score (Table 1)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Provides a balanced harmonic mean of precision and recall, useful for uneven class distributions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: TP, FP, FN (and TN in the confusion-matrix row) = dimensionless non-negative integer counts of matches, unit [1 = one match]; 'Current Predictions' = count of correct predictions, unit [1] — printed verbatim as 'Current Predictions' in the Table 1 image on PDF p.4 (journal p.247), an apparent typo for 'Correct Predictions' since the purpose column says 'Measures the overall percentage of correct predictions'; 'Total Predictions' = total predictions made, unit [1]; Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score = dimensionless ratios in [0,1] (count/count, hence dimensionally homogeneous); the constant 2 and the operator 'x' (multiplication, printed as lowercase x) are dimensionless. ROC-AUC is described as one-vs-rest across thresholds (PDF p.5) with no formula printed; it is a dimensionless ranking probability in [0,1].
primitives.assumptions: As printed (Table 1, PDF pp.4-5, journal pp.247-248): Precision evaluates 'exactness' and Recall 'completeness' per outcome; F1 is the harmonic mean for uneven class distributions; ROC-AUC uses a one-vs-rest approach for the three classes; the confusion matrix gives True Positives vs False Positives breakdowns. Formulas for Precision, Recall, F1 are embedded images transcribed at 600 DPI; Accuracy is printed with words rather than TP/TN symbols; ROC-AUC and Confusion Matrix formula cells are blank in the source.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularities: Precision undefined when TP+FP=0; Recall undefined when TP+FN=0; F1 undefined (0/0) when Precision+Recall=0. Accuracy is misleading under class imbalance (a draw-heavy or home-heavy league). The harmonic mean makes F1 veto-sensitive: a near-zero recall collapses F1 regardless of precision. Critically, threshold-free ROC-AUC can read near 1.0 while argmax accuracy stays moderate when leaked features rank outcomes almost perfectly but probability mass is misallocated — exactly the 99.00% vs 87.14% pattern reported in Table 3.
timescales: tau_3 = metrics computed once on the held-out test season

layer2.mapping: Precision and Recall are asymmetric loss weights on the confusion matrix of any 22-player outcome classifier; the F1 harmonic mean is a veto-weighted aggregation kernel: the weaker of exactness/completeness dominates the score, which is the same algebraic shape as a cross-layer veto where the binding constraint overrides the favorable one. In GSE scoring, per-class recall on the tail class (draw / upset) is the quantity that protects a DFS portfolio, not aggregate accuracy.
layer2.telemetry: Per-class TP/FP/FN/TN counts on the temporal test set; per-class F1 (not just macro accuracy); calibration of the probability outputs before any decision weighting; ablation-recomputed AUC to detect leakage-driven ranking inflation.

primitives.name: Reported performance claims under audit: RF 87.14% / ROC-AUC 99.00%, internal ranking contradiction, leakage red flag
primitives.verbatim_quote: It achieved an overall accuracy of 87.14%, with a precision of 86.70% and a recall of 84.70%. The F1-score was 84.92%, and the ROC-AUC was 99.00%
primitives.assumptions: As printed (PDF p.7, journal p.250, Random Forest results; Table 3 on PDF p.5): metrics are percentages on the held-out test split. The abstract (PDF p.1) and comparative analysis (PDF p.8) rank Random Forest first; the conclusion (PDF p.9) states 'The results showed that XGBoost achieved better performance, followed by lightGB and Random Forest.' The narrative on PDF p.8 also claims XGBoost 'significantly outperformed the Random Forest benchmark' while reporting 86.64% accuracy against RF's 87.14%. Dataset attributes (PDF p.5) explicitly include 'Scoring Data: Full-time and Half-time goals/results (Home Win, Away Win, Draw)'; the preprocessing section removes 'irrelevant features, such as match IDs' but never states that full-time scoring columns were excluded from the feature matrix.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Three independent failure signatures. (1) Internal contradiction: abstract/results rank RF first, conclusion ranks XGBoost first, and the 'significantly outperformed' prose contradicts its own numbers (86.64 < 87.14) — ranking claims are inadmissible until reconciled against Table 3. (2) Leakage red flag: one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 99.00% alongside 87.14% accuracy is anomalous for three-way football outcomes and is consistent with target information (full-time goals) entering features; full-time goals are a deterministic function of the target. (3) No calibration, no confidence intervals, no trivial-baseline comparison, and no ablation are reported. Per doctrine these numbers enter the foundry only as quoted, flagged claims — never as win-rate headlines — and no sportsbook odds are used anywhere in this extraction or its mappings (odds-based studies appear only in the paper's literature review).
timescales: test window = most recent 15% of seasons

layer2.mapping: This primitive is the audit invariant itself: a headline metric without an information-boundary audit is not evidence. It binds directly to GSE's no-win-rate-headlines doctrine and to the 22-player system's state-estimation rule that no feature may carry information from after the prediction timestamp. The AUC-vs-accuracy divergence is a reusable telemetry signature of target leakage in any outcome model, football or otherwise.
layer2.telemetry: Feature-availability timestamps; ablation of full-time/half-time scoring columns followed by recomputed AUC and accuracy; reconciliation of prose ranking claims against the numeric table; per-class draw recall as the canary for three-way overconfidence.

reasoning_traces.think: The sovereign fact of this paper is not its headline accuracy but the information boundary it never audits. Start from the reported invariant: Random Forest at 87.14% accuracy with a one-vs-rest ROC-AUC of 99.00% on a temporal test split of five EPL seasons. AUC measures ranking quality across all thresholds; accuracy measures the quality of the single argmax decision. In a genuinely noisy three-way outcome process, near-perfect ranking coexisting with mediocre decisions is an anomalous signature. The most parsimonious explanation is that some feature encodes the target itself. The paper's own dataset description supplies the candidate: 'Scoring Data: Full-time and Half-time goals/results' are listed as dataset attributes, and full-time goals are a deterministic function of the Home/Draw/Away target. The preprocessing section says irrelevant features 'such as match IDs' were removed, but it never states that full-time scoring columns were excluded from the feature matrix. Half-time goals are legitimately usable at halftime; full-time goals are not usable before kickoff. Until an ablation removes those columns and recomputes AUC, the 99.00% figure is inadmissible as calibration telemetry. This is the foundry's core discipline: the number is a quoted claim under audit, never a win-rate headline, and the audit protocol — not the metric — is the reusable primitive. Second, the temporal split is the correct skeleton and is exactly isomorphic to GSE held-out discipline: no fit is scored on its own training rows, and the test window must be strictly later than every training row. But the paper layers stratification on top of the temporal split, forcing win/draw/loss proportions to match across eras. That quietly assumes class-proportion stationarity across seasons, which sits in tension with the paper's own framing of the EPL as volatile and rapidly evolving. Stratification is not wrong in principle, but it is an assumption that must be tested against per-season class counts, not asserted. Third, the manuscript contradicts itself in a way that is itself evidence. The abstract and the comparative analysis rank Random Forest first; the conclusion ranks XGBoost first; and the results narrative claims XGBoost 'significantly outperformed' Random Forest while reporting 86.64% against 87.14%. Retrocausally, this is the scar of layered drafting: the conclusion was almost certainly written against an earlier version of the results table and never reconciled. For the foundry, the lesson generalizes: prose ranking claims are belief states; the numeric table is the invariant. When they disagree, the disagreement is the signal, and the artifact must record both rather than silently picking a winner. Fourth, the lineage is real and must not be fabricated: the paper cites Breiman (2001) for Random Forest and Friedman (2001) for gradient boosting, and its own historical account runs from mid-20th-century statistical recording through opti-tracking and GPS vests to ensemble ML. Precision, recall, and F1 are standard classification metrics printed in Table 1; they have no football origin and none is invented here. Finally, the odds boundary: the literature review discusses odds-using studies (Mittal et al. 2020; Wunderlich and Memmert 2016), but this extraction adopts no odds as inputs anywhere, in keeping with held-out discipline. The paper's own cited literature concedes that boosting 'competitive with bookmaker predictions' came 'without consistently guaranteeing profit' — a reminder that classification accuracy and decision value are different quantities, and the foundry maps distributions, not picks.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The paper's own genealogy (PDF p.2) runs from mid-20th-century statistical recording of goals, shots, and possession, through the digital big-data era of opti-tracking cameras and GPS vests, to ensemble ML. The historical scar it names is the failure of static-data models to adapt to transfers, injuries, and coaching changes (citing Baboota and Kaur 2018). Two hidden states shaped this artifact: the dataset's full-time scoring columns, inherited from football-data.co.uk's standard schema, and the manuscript's layered drafting, which left the abstract ranking RF first while the conclusion ranked XGBoost first. The algorithmic lineage is Breiman (2001) and Friedman (2001), cited in the references — no football-era origin is fabricated for these methods.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Model the belief clash recursively. The authors believe the ensemble 'enhanced prediction consistency' and that 87.14% accuracy demonstrates effectiveness; the conclusion's author believes XGBoost won; each anticipates the reader will accept the table without cross-checking the prose. A skeptical reviewer, seeing 99.00% AUC, believes leakage until ablation proves otherwise. The industry audience believes high accuracy converts to profit, a belief the paper's own cited literature contradicts ('without consistently guaranteeing profit'). The foundry auditor models all three minds at once and trusts none of their headline claims: the auditor's invariant is the information boundary, and every belief state must submit to it before any number is allowed to calibrate a downstream model.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The binding veto here is epistemic physics: no feature may carry information from after the prediction timestamp. This constraint overrides any accuracy gain, however large — a 99.00% AUC produced by leaked full-time goals is not a better model, it is a broken measurement, and it is vetoed as a calibration input regardless of its apparent expected value. The same veto applies to the prose: a ranking claim that contradicts its own numeric table cannot propagate into the foundry's state. Only after ablation and reconciliation may the surviving metrics re-enter as telemetry.

reasoning_traces.think: The second reusable structure is the observation kernel. The paper computes rolling averages of goals, shots, and possession over the last 3, 5, and 10 matches, plus attack/defence ratios, head-to-head records, home-ground advantage, and days since last match as a fatigue proxy. Read sovereignly, the three window lengths are not three features but three bias-variance settings on one latent state: team strength. A 3-match window tracks fast regime changes (new manager, key injury) with high variance; a 10-match window is stable but stale after a transfer window; the 5-match window is the compromise. This is a multi-scale low-pass filter on a hidden state, and the correct foundry abstraction is the kernel family, not any single window. The breakdown regime is the paper's own stated one: static or slow-updating features fail when the underlying state jumps. Days-since-last-match is the most interesting primitive because it is a scalar recovery clock standing in for a high-dimensional physiological process. Glycogen resynthesis and muscle repair run on roughly 24-72 hour timescales depending on load; a congested fixture list with midweek European travel compresses recovery below that window, and travel plus circadian disruption adds load that a day-count cannot see. So the proxy is directionally right but dimensionally impoverished: it needs calibration against minutes played, GPS high-speed running distance, and travel logs before it can gate anything. In the 22-player dynamical system, the binding is explicit: state x_t carries latent strength and fatigue for both sides, the rolling features are the observation model, and the classifier approximates the transition kernel P(Home/Draw/Away | x_t). Fatigue must discount effective strength before the kernel is evaluated, otherwise the model systematically overrates congested squads. The same structure transfers to GSE's Coach-Mind sim: rolling opponent-tendency priors are the observation kernel on the coordinator's latent play-calling policy, and a fatigue gate on the quarterback or offensive line discounts the EV of deep-dropback or high-volume run scripts. The bagging layer adds a second invariant: averaging independent trees reduces variance, exactly as averaging independent simulation draws reduces scenario noise — and both fail the same way when the draws are correlated through a shared dominant feature or a shared prior. The probability outputs are vote fractions, not calibrated posteriors; the paper reports no reliability diagram, so a calibration layer is mandatory before any portfolio weighting. The draw class is the structural tail: three-way classifiers systematically under-predict it, and F1's harmonic mean is the algebraic veto that punishes a precision-heavy classifier for missing that tail. For DFS and portfolio tail risk, per-class draw recall — not aggregate accuracy — is the protective quantity, and the distribution must remain LINE-FREE: no odds inputs, no published picks, internal artifacts only. The cross-layer veto completes the loop: when the model's win probability is high but the recovery clock says two days since a midweek away fixture, physiology vetoes the high-press lineup the model's features implicitly recommend; when a short-week quarterback carries a shoulder limitation, biomechanics vetoes the deep-pass script regardless of modeled EV. The high-EV call is admissible only after every lower layer has declined to veto it.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The rolling-form idea descends from the paper's own account of football's quantitative turn: mid-20th-century match recording made goals, shots, and possession countable, and tracking-era data made them available at match granularity. The fatigue proxy descends from fixture congestion in the modern calendar, where midweek European competition compresses recovery between league matches. The hidden state the proxy fails to capture is accumulated physical load and travel burden — the scar of a schedule built for broadcast revenue rather than physiology. Breiman's bagging (2001) supplies the variance-reduction lineage; none of these methods has a fabricated football origin.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Recursive belief clash under pressure: the manager's comfort call is to start the in-form striker the model's rolling features endorse; the opposing analyst anticipates that comfort and sets a press trap keyed to the fatigued fullback the day-count proxy cannot see; the quarterback's internal clock — in the GSE transfer of this structure — clashes with the coordinator's tendency, because the QB knows his shoulder limits the deep progression the tendency call assumes. Each mind models the next: the manager models the analyst modeling the manager. The model sits outside this recursion and must not be trusted to resolve it; only the fatigue and injury telemetry can break the loop, which is why the veto layer sits below the decision layer.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Physiology vetoes the high-EV call: two days since a midweek away fixture, with GPS high-speed running load still elevated, means the high-press game plan implied by the model's strength features is inadmissible even when P(home win) is high — the recovery clock gates the transition kernel before any decision is scored. In the GSE transfer, a short-week quarterback with a shoulder limitation vetoes the deep-dropback script regardless of modeled EV, and a cold-venue grip constraint vetoes the ball-security-negative pass concept. The rule is invariant: the favorable layer proposes, the binding physical layer disposes, and no EV calculation may override a violated physiological or biomechanical constraint.

universal_lens: The polymath audit lens this book trains is information-boundary auditing: any predictive claim is a claim about what was knowable at prediction time, so the first question is never 'how accurate?' but 'which features could carry post-target information?' Second, treat prose-versus-table contradictions as first-class signal, not editorial noise — the disagreement localizes the hidden state of the artifact's production. Third, every metric is a loss-weighting choice: accuracy hides class imbalance, AUC hides calibration, and the harmonic mean is a veto algebra. These three habits transfer unchanged to physiology, finance, and any dynamical-system identification task.
gsi_mapping: Days-since-last-match is a scalar stand-in for bioenergetic recovery: glycogen resynthesis and muscle repair on roughly 24-72 hour timescales, calibratable against minutes played, GPS high-speed running distance, heart-rate variability, and creatine kinase telemetry. The rolling-window kernel maps to acute-versus-chronic load monitoring, where short windows flag spikes and long windows establish baseline capacity. The hard availability veto — concussion protocol, axonal shear risk, hamstring load limits — sits below any performance model exactly as the fatigue gate sits below the outcome kernel: clinical telemetry can forbid participation regardless of modeled performance, and no performance metric may override a clinical constraint.
gse_mapping: For Coach-Mind simulation, rolling 3/5/10-match form becomes rolling opponent-tendency priors on the coordinator's latent policy, and the temporal split becomes the held-out rule that no fit is scored on its own training rows. The bagging variance-reduction invariant maps to averaging independent simulation scenarios, with correlated priors breaking it the same way a leaked feature breaks tree independence. Output is a LINE-FREE outcome distribution, never a pick; per-class draw/upset recall is the DFS portfolio tail-risk guard, and F1's harmonic mean is the veto algebra that punishes ignoring the tail. No sportsbook odds enter any layer; artifacts stay internal and are never published.
